{{recipesummary | Category = Fermented food recipes | Servings = 8 | Time = Prep: 15 minutes
Fermentation: 2–3 days | Image = [[File:Salsa ferment.jpg|300px]] | Rating = 2 }} __NOTOC__ {{recipe}} | [[:Category:Fermented food recipes|Fermented food recipes]] This '''[[Cookbook:Fermentation|fermented]] salsa''' recipe produces a tangy tomato sauce with strong flavour. No cooking is required. ==Ingredients== [[Image:Salsa ferment ingredients.jpg|thumb|The ingredients.|327x327px]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] (2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) fresh [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] * 1 large [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|capsicum]] (bell pepper) * 3–6 fresh [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]] * 1 fresh [[Cookbook:Onion|red onion]] * 3–4 cloves of [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]] * 1 bunch of fresh [[Cookbook:cilantro|cilantro]] (coriander leaf, Chinese parsley) * 1–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] non-iodised [[Cookbook:salt|salt]] * [[Cookbook:Spices and herbs|spices]] to taste (optional) ==Procedure== # Clean and dry a large (1 litre) preserves jar and a large bowl # [[Cookbook:Dice|Dice]] the tomatoes # Quarter and [[Cookbook:Slicing|slice]] the capsicum # Finely slice the chilis, removing the seeds if you prefer. Make sure to wash your hands right after cutting the chilis, and DO NOT touch your eyes or face for some time after handling the chilis—if you do, the chili juice residue could cause a very painful burning sensation.) # Peel and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chop]] the onion and garlic finely. Roughly chop the cilantro. # Mix all ingredients together in the bowl with salt and (optional) spices; mix well! # Pack tightly into the jar, leaving 1 cm space at the top. # Cover the jar with a cloth or [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|cling-wrap]]. Sit the jar in a bowl or on a plate, so that any juice that might overflow will be collected and won't make a mess. Leave to ferment at room temperature. # The salsa will be fermented in 2–3 days, depending on the climate. Wipe any excess liquid from around the jar, and put the lid on tightly before moving it to the refrigerator. It will last well in the fridge, but will continue to slowly ferment, getting more sour as time passes. ==Notes, tips, and variations== *With the above fresh ingredients, there should be enough microbial load for the salsa to start fermenting by itself. Bubbles will begin rising to the top of the jar, showing that fermentation is under way—you should be able to see this through the side of the jar. Don't seal the jar while it is fermenting, as it will build up gas pressure and might break the jar. If you are concerned that fermentation will not start by itself, you can add a starter culture. A good starter culture is a little juice from a recently-fermented [[Cookbook:sauerkraut|sauerkraut]] or [[Cookbook:kimchi|kimchi]], as this will bring across the necessary lactic acid bacteria and yeasts. *This is best within a few days, unless you like it quite sour! *The salt used should be non-iodised salt if possible (e.g. pickling salt, kosher salt). This is because the iodine in iodised table salt will inhibit the fermentation a little. Use what you've got, but best results will be obtained without the iodine. *Use fresh ingredients where possible; if you do use canned or dried ingredients, you may need to use a starter (see above). *This recipe prefers to ferment at a temperature between 18–22°C (64–72°F). It will happily ferment outside that range, but if you want to keep it in that range, there are some tips available on the [[Cookbook:Fermentation#Temperature|fermentation page]]. *There is a suggestion on the [[{{TALKPAGENAME}}|talk page]] that more salt is required; read the discussion and decide for yourself, but traditional French recipes add no salt during the fermentation of crushed tomatoes. Salt volume recommendations made without specifying brand (and therefore grain size and shape) are not precise in any case. ==Warnings== *When handling hot chilis, use gloves or take extra care to keep your hands away from eyes and other sensitive areas ''even after washing them''.
